column8: What the live build does today
Site accepts negative area and voltage (1-11)

column5: Grants site access, shares load data

column8: Accepts a future assessment date (1-09)

column5: Create proposal — cost build-up, markups, contingency, yield
column8: Annual lease figure multiplies roof area by a per-kilowatt-hour rate — out by ~182× (§3.3 of the sweep analysis)
RC-A the raiser can approve their own request
No confirmation; one mis-click sends a commercial document (1-20)
Register: G7 is specified as markup more than five points below policy — a conditional gate. The code raises it on every won decision

column6: opportunities → won · or back to proposing
column8: RC-A

column5: Automatic: project created, proposal frozen, eight risk terms seeded
column6: projects → setup · proposals → frozen · risk_terms × 8 → not_yet_read

column5: Create contract — type, value, retention, warranty
column8: Contract record stays draft forever; nothing on the Contract tab can sign it (1-14)

column5: Attach signed contract document and date
column8: G9 is specified but no code raises it. Signed date accepts 31 December 2027 and immediately unlocks the setup gate (1-08)

column5: Acknowledge the eight risk terms; contract risk review
column8: G10 is specified but no code raises it. The schema carries a riskReviewOutcome (approved · proceeded without review · rejected) that nothing sets. Terms display no text, so acknowledgement is uninformed (1-23)

column5: Assign project parties — ten seat roles from Project Manager to Client Representative
column8: assignProjectParty exists as a mutation; no control in the interface (1-04)
Enforced. But the live HB6 row describes a different rule (RC-N); the enforcement here is a stage check, not the named block

column5: Create design package — one of ten disciplines
Add deliverables — nine types, from layout plan to commissioning checklist
Record professional seal — engineer, licence, expiry, discipline
column8: Recorded, then never displayed back. No badge on the deliverable, and a second contradictory seal can be added on top (2-13)
A deliverable can go straight from draft to approved by the person who drew it. in_review can be skipped and no reviewer is named (2-06)
Refused unless the package is at issued_for_approval — a correct precondition
RC-A the raiser can approve their own request
This is the one gate fully enforced in the product. updateDesignPackage refuses to set issued_for_construction without an approved gate 18
Item code is free text, not a picker from the catalogue. Nothing checks a line against stock on hand (2-02)
A negative default duration is accepted, so a permit type can expire before it is issued (1-17). The library ships empty, so every customer types the same Philippine permit set from memory (2-28)

column5: Automatic: requirement observed — the library accumulates
column8: The raw field name timesObserved is printed to the user (1-18). The behaviour is correct — this is L5, accumulate rather than maintain — only the wording is wrong
Refused unless the permit is in draft
G20 is specified but no code raises it anywhere. The only occurrence of gate 20 in the whole codebase is the seed definition
Correctly refused unless the permit is approved

column5: The approved permit is what mobilisation checks for
column8: HB4 fires in Part 5, not here

column5: Create the purchase order against a project and a supplier
column8: The order number is PO-YYYYMM-nnn, counted from orders on that project, so two projects in the same month both produce PO-202609-001

column5: Add order lines, each optionally linked to a bill of materials line
column8: The link is optional, and material readiness only counts linked lines
Correctly refused unless the order has at least one line

column7: G4 ≤ ₱100,000 · Procurement Head · Director · 2 days — G5 > ₱100,000 · Director · Chief Operating Officer · 2 days
column8: The approval is not real. The browser sends manual-<timestamp> as the approval reference. No approval request is created, no approver is named, no role is checked, and the amount is never looked at

column5: Issue the order to the supplier — committed cost begins
column8: HB6 is checked here, and passes on any non-empty reference

Nothing enters stock. Delivered quantity above ordered quantity is accepted. accepted + rejected is never checked against delivered. The three inspection statuses — accepted, partially accepted, rejected — cannot be reached: no mutation sets them
Correct

column5: Automatic: material readiness — computed on read, never stored
column8: Counts only order lines linked to a bill of materials line. An unlinked line reads as zero readiness however much has arrived
Does not exist. The schema reserves gate5ApprovalId for it; no mutation writes that field. An issued order is frozen — the error says "Use an amendment (Gate 5)" and there is nothing to use

column5: A second person confirms the account
column8: Enforced. The person who added the account cannot confirm it. Adding a new account supersedes the old one

column5: Maintain locations and the item catalogue — seven categories
column8: Item code and location code are unique, and correctly refused on collision

column5: Create a stock transfer — four directions
column8: Source and destination must differ; at least one line required. Both correct
No stock check. Dispatching more than exists drives on-hand negative with no warning. Neither gate is raised anywhere

The shortfall vanishes. In-transit is reduced by the dispatched quantity, on-hand is increased by the received quantity, and the difference is written off silently — no quarantine, no variance record, no adjustment raised

column5: Raise a stock adjustment — write up or write off
column8: Quantity must be positive. Correct
The only same-person refusal in the platform. "You cannot approve your own adjustment (Gate 26)"

column5: Open a physical count — stock is snapshotted into count lines
column8: lockDate is stored and locks nothing — transfers and adjustments can move stock while the count is open. G27 has no code anywhere. Only items that already have a stock position are snapshotted, so material physically present but never recorded cannot be counted in
Every variance is written straight into stock with no approval at all. The same person can open, submit and close it
HB5 — quarantined material cannot be issued. The quarantined quantity is never set by any code, so the block can never fire
A request can be declined but never formally accepted — allocation happens by deploying against it
The workforce person is marked deployed and the request allocation advances. Nothing checks they are at this project's site
Checks only that the deployment is planned. HB1 insurance certificate and HB4 prerequisite permit belong here and neither exists in code
Assign and return only. No condition on return, no calibration date, no operator

column5: Automatic: the project stage should become construction
column8: The only stage mutation in the platform is setup → design. No code sets a project to procurement, construction, commissioning or handover. A project can never leave design

column5: Open the site report for the day
column8: One per project per day, correctly refused on a duplicate. A date in the future is accepted. createdOnDevice is recorded but never surfaced

column5: Record the toolbox meeting and who attended
column8: photographRef is in the schema and no screen uses it — the toolbox photograph cannot be attached

column5: Add the day's activities against blocks
column8: Every activity must name a block — correct. Cumulative percent complete is never checked against the previous entry, so progress can go backwards without comment
Refused without a toolbox meeting. The one enforced safety precondition in this part
No role check and no same-person check — the person who submitted can approve

column5: Automatic: block completion computed on read
column8: Correct — never stored. This is L5 working as designed

column5: Automatic: days worked derived from toolbox attendance
column8: Correct, and important. Presence is never tracked; a person is paid for a day because their name is on that day's toolbox meeting

column5: The Department of Labor and Employment approves the Construction Safety and Health Program
column8: No code checks it, and the programme has no record in the platform at all — there is nowhere to file the approval

column5: Create a permit to work — six types
column8: The issuer is supplied by the caller, not taken from the person acting. The same-day rule the schema promises is not enforced, and expired is unreachable — no code ever sets it

No Safety Officer check. issuePermitToWork verifies only that the permit is a draft. Anyone signed in can issue a hot-work or confined-space permit. The competency list the schema names does not exist anywhere

column5: Any person raises a safety stop
column8: Correct. Any person may raise it and the actor is recorded from the session
No Safety Officer check and no same-person check. The person who raised the stop can lift it. The clearance note is optional
The statutory deadline is typed by hand, never derived from type or severity
Genuinely anonymous. There is no reporter field on the record at all — not hidden, absent. Correct, and rare
Findings are free text
Must link to an incident or an inspection — enforced. The five levels of the hierarchy of controls are recorded properly
Transitions are validated against a state table — correct
The approval reference is a string the caller supplies. The same pattern as gate 4: the check is that the string is not empty

column5: Automatic: no project reaches commissioning with an open report
column8: The mutation the schema names does not exist. And there is no block B0 — the spine starts at Mobilization, and blocks have no status, so "B0 signed off" is not a state anything can be in

column5: Create a billing milestone on the contract

column8: Percent complete is derived from block activities and cannot be typed — correct, and one of the better pieces of design in the platform. The claimed amount is checked against nothing: not the contract value, not the milestone, not the percent complete

column5: Submit the claim to the client
column8: The code raises gate 25a, which the specification reserves for inter-island inventory transfers. The approval reference is a string the caller supplies and it is not even checked for emptiness
The code raises gate 25b. Certified is correctly a separate field from claimed — and is never compared to it, so a claim of ₱1,000,000 can be certified at ₱9,000,000
The paid amount is not checked against the certified amount

column5: Raise the retention invoice at the release date
column8: Does not exist. There is no retention invoice record anywhere. Retention percent and release months are stored on the contract and a release date is derived at turnover — and nothing bills it

Enforced, and well written. "Hard Block 6: Fund request FR-… is released but not yet liquidated. Liquidate the outstanding advance before raising a new request." It names the block, the condition and the release
No role check, no same-person check. The approved amount is not bounded by the requested amount
The person who approved can release. Two of the three cash controls are the same person
A liquidation reference is required — correct. Nothing checks what it points at, and there is no amount
The gate is derived at creation, from severity
The gate is read from severity, not from the amount. gateIdForSeverity maps minor→1, moderate→2, major→3. A ₱5,000,000 write-off marked minor raises gate 1
The mutation exists and no screen calls it — the whole variation order feature is reachable only through the protocol

No approve mutation exists. gate9ApprovalId is never written by anything, so the value adjustment reaches nothing. The schema comment calls this gate 9; the specification says gate 9 is the signed customer agreement and gate 8 is the variation order — the two are swapped
A gated line must carry a gate — correctly refused otherwise. The three bands are exactly as specified

column5: Automatic: three-month gap detected on read
column8: Correct. Three consecutive future months with no secured or gated line. Computed, never stored
There is no accounts payable. No supplier invoice, no subcontractor invoice, no payment, no remittance. The forecast covers cash in only
Optionally linked to a resource request from Part 5
Retention expiry is diarised on the candidate — correct
The record is hidden from the candidate until it is submitted — correct

column5: Record the approval and issue the offer
column8: The reference is required and trimmed — stricter than gates 11, 19 and 23. But G24 in the specification is Role Assignment, not an offer
The candidate status moves to hired or rejected in the same transaction — correct
The employee record is separate from the person record, and nothing links a hired candidate to it. Someone re-types the name

column5: Automatic: regularisation diarised at six months
column8: A diary entry, never an automatic conversion. Exactly right — the platform reminds, a person decides

column5: An employee requests leave — seven types

column8: No same-person check — an employee can approve their own leave. An over-application clamps the balance to zero rather than refusing, so ten days taken against a four-day balance silently becomes four

column5: The employee writes their own objectives
column8: Written by the person, not set for them — correct

column5: Quarterly review — self assessment, manager review, acknowledgement
column8: Reasons are required and there is no numeric score — correct. A three-step review with the employee acknowledging at the end

Fully anonymous. No person is stored, and no audit entry is written either — the code says so in a comment, because an audit row would break the anonymity. This is the most careful piece of privacy design in the platform

column5: Enter the four statutory rate tables and their brackets
column8: Three bracket shapes: fixed, percentage, graduated. Correct for Philippine contributions and Bureau of Internal Revenue bands

Refused without at least one bracket; the previous approved table is superseded in the same transaction. Both correct. The code names this G32, which the specification reserves for Role Permission Change, and nothing checks that a Finance role approves
An overlapping open period is correctly refused
Article 116 honoured: there is no remove mutation at all. A days adjustment needs a reason of at least ten characters

Refused unless all four tables are approved, with a message naming all four. The table versions are locked to the period on the first run and stamped on every line. Nothing compares the three runs — it is a count, not a reconciliation

column7: G30 · Chief Operating Officer · no alternate
column8: Three runs are required first — enforced. G30 in the specification is Incident Investigation Closure
Refused unless the period is approved — correct. Signature, biometric or witness

column7: G31 · Head of Finance · no alternate
column8: G31 in the specification is Threshold and Configuration Change

column5: The protocol can set any status directly
column8: toolUpdatePayrollPeriod writes the status straight through, and stamps disbursedAt and disbursedBy when it does
Completion is computed from site activities — correct. The project stage still cannot move; it is stuck in design from Part 5
There is no acceptance record. No certificate, no signature, no date, nothing to attach
G21 has no code anywhere. recordTurnoverDate is ungated and any signed-in person can call it

column5: Automatic: retention release and warranty expiry derived
column8: Both dates are derived from the contract in a single transaction — correct, and one of the cleanest pieces of code in the product

column5: Raise the retention invoice at the release date
column8: No record exists — Part 6. The release date is derived correctly and then nothing reads it
Frequency in calendar days; a next visit date is set once
Refused after warranty expiry, with a readable message naming the date. The schema calls this hard block 5 — a fourth meaning of that number

column5: Work the visit — nine activity types
column8: Three outcomes per activity: satisfactory, requires attention, not applicable
Reading type and unit are free text. Energy, irradiation and performance ratio are not a fixed list, so nothing can be trended reliably

column6: om_defects → open → acknowledged → in_repair → resolved · escalated
column8: Four severities and five states — and no gate on escalation, including for a critical defect
A real approval request, built from the gate row with the approver role copied onto it. This is the right pattern and one of only three places it is used
Approved by its own patch: no R6 refusal and no role check. The field is gate30ApprovalId, the request is raised against gate 34, and the specification calls neither of them a service report sign-off

column5: Automatic: the next visit date advances
column8: Never happens. The schema says it is updated after each visit and no code does it. Nothing ever falls due
There is no warranty claim record anywhere. warranty_claim exists only as a document category in the file module. The gate reserved for it is being consumed by the visit sign-off at 8.12
